page: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_MI300X_v5 is an isolated, accelerator-focused instance type within the NDISv5MI300X family, engineered specifically for large-scale artificial intelligence models and high-performance computing workloads. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture supplying 96 dedicated vCPUs managed under Microsoft Hyper-V. In addition to high-density host compute, the platform integrates 1850.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 19.27 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by 8 AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs featuring a combined total of 1536 GB of high-bandwidth GPU memory. Complementing the compute and accelerator stack, the instance includes 31820 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and incorporates RDMA networking capabilities alongside support for Premium Storage. Public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

The vast memory footprint across both system RAM and GPU VRAM, paired with 31.8 TB of fast local NVMe storage, makes the instance effective for distributed deep learning training, massive LLM inference, and data-intensive computational simulations without external storage bottlenecks. While the specialized multi-GPU architecture commands a premium hardware profile, the consolidation of massive VRAM and local I/O capacity yields high resource density for demanding AI clusters.
description: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_MI300X_v5 is an isolated GPU-accelerated server built for large-scale AI and high-performance computing. Operating on an x86_64 Intel platform managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 1850.0 GB of system memory, yielding 19.27 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by an array of 8 AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs with 1536 GB of aggregate VRAM. Local data persistence and caching are handled by 31820 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD storage. The platform is also RDMA-capable and supports Premium Storage configurations, making it suited for memory-intensive machine learning workloads, including multi-billion parameter model training, large language model inference, and distributed data processing frameworks requiring substantial local storage throughput.
